findings.topic: Original transfer admission and sender state
findings.detail: The actual reading/closing/closed members alone determine eligibility. A stopped read's current_read pointer adds no new prohibition. Native packet allocation precedes the sole closed=true mutation. No descriptor reset, read-offset mutation, AfterClose/EOF, stream retirement or async-context transfer is added. Same-live-Engine checks are stated host entry preconditions.

findings.topic: Descriptor ownership and original zero/stdio boundaries
findings.detail: The opaque C++ owner stores its real int fd and mandatory function addresses. Its original strict fd>0 gate remains exact, including fd0 behavior. Within it the actual canonical caller-stack uv_fs_t, CHECK_NE, begin trace, uv_fs_close(nullptr,...,nullptr), CHECK_EQ zero, end trace and request cleanup retain their order. Both null-callback platform paths are synchronous and do not register a queued request. Windows fs__close's fd<=2 handling is preserved. Controls deliberately use fd>2; they do not claim runtime evidence for stdio or fatal CHECK paths.

The allocation prefix atomically charges and independently retains the native memory domain. Engine context/runtime teardown precedes release of its own owner reference, leaving the packet's prefix valid. Delete frees its allocation then releases that exact charge/reference without dereferencing Engine, Environment, service or lease. Process-lifetime trace function addresses carry no captured raw data. They must consult actual global tracing at invocation; the unresolved production owner is not replaced by the labeled test observers.

All four actual C ABI functions declare DiagnosticContextScope as the first local. Create nests AllocationScope inside it; native new-handler/bad_alloc policy remains native. Borrowed context is synchronous only. NULL masks any outer admission and restores it on return, including after Engine retirement and on a different thread. Packet stores no JSContext.

findings.topic: Unique packet consumption and actual receiver construction
findings.detail: Owned.move/deinit clear the original slot before further ownership work. Deserialize consumes the caller slot immediately and defers actual packet deletion. Missing actual weak BindingData returns null and closes fd>0. Otherwise take writes packet fd=-1 before genuine absent-object Handle.create with absent offset/length overrides. A failed later constructor does not restore packet descriptor ownership, matching the original order. The control fixture explicitly adopts that abandoned descriptor for cleanup without changing production. It preserves the missing-full-template error and does not fabricate a receiver.

findings.topic: Actual StrongHandle edge and fixture roots
findings.detail: Successful construction strengthens the same native State/persistent before the caller scope retires. clone increments that same native reference; move clears the old edge; deinit clears its slot before the last release can destroy the Handle or return its persistent to weak. StrongHandle is receiver-thread-only. The separate native packet alone crosses a real thread, and test observations are read after join. Fixture-owned Controller, Queue and duplicated handle-key roots remain live after sender collection, so the borrowed receive inputs do not rely on a destroyed Handle; their release occurs in fixture teardown.
